docs.title: valigo
docs.text:
valigo is a validation library for Go structs. Rules are configured once, in code, by pointers to the fields of a model: b.String(&u.Name).Required().MaxLen(64). The compiler checks that a rule fits the field type and that its arguments have the field type, the validation itself doesn't allocate on valid objects, and error messages are translated.

One-line ideology

Rules are Go code next to the struct, not strings in tags: a typo or a wrong type doesn't compile.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
go get github.com/insei/valigo@latest

Minimum Go version is 1.27: the configurator uses generic methods.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "regexp"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
)

type User struct {
    Name  string
    Email string
    Age   int
    Phone *string
    Tags  []string
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[User](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[User], u *User) {
        b.String(&u.Name).Trim().Required().MaxLen(64)
        b.String(&u.Email).Required().Email()
        b.Number(&u.Age).AnyOfInterval(18, 120)
        b.String(&u.Phone).Regexp(regexp.MustCompile(`^\+\d{10,15}$`)) // a nil phone is skipped
        b.StringSlice(&u.Tags).MaxLen(5).Each(func(tag *str.BaseConfigurator) {
            tag.Trim().Required().MaxLen(16)
        })
    })

    user := &User{Name: "  Ann  ", Email: "ann.example.com", Age: 16, Tags: []string{"go", " "}}
    for _, err := range v.Validate(context.Background(), user) {
        fmt.Println(err)
    }
    fmt.Printf("%q\n", user.Name)
}

Output:

Should be email address (Email: ann.example.com)
Only interval[18 - 120] is allowed (Age: 16)
Should be fulfilled (Tags[1]: )
"Ann"

What happens here:

  1. valigo.New() creates a validator with the English and Russian messages.
  2. valigo.Configure[User] calls the function once with a model: a *User whose nested pointer structs are allocated. Rules are bound to the fields of the model by their pointers, &u.Name.
  3. Every configurator method returns the configurator of the field, so rules are chained. They run in the order of the chain: Trim changes the value before Required checks it.
  4. v.Validate runs the rules of the *User type and returns nil for a valid object. Every error has the message, the location of the field (Tags[1] for the element of a slice) and the value.

docs.title: For AI agents
docs.text: AI agents often write the code that uses a library, and a model trained before the typed configurator doesn't know its API: it writes Number(&u.Score) for a *int field or Max(int64(5)) with an any argument. Give the agent the current documentation.

docs.title: The skill
docs.text:
skills/valigo/SKILL.md is a short guide for agents in the Agent Skills format: the rules, complete programs, the configurators with their rules and the common mistakes. It is versioned with the code, and CI builds and runs its programs against the code of the repository, so it doesn't describe the API that doesn't exist.

Claude Code finds the skill in the .claude/skills directory of the project or of the user:

mkdir -p .claude/skills/valigo
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Insei/valigo/main/skills/valigo/SKILL.md \
  -o .claude/skills/valigo/SKILL.md

Replace main with the release tag to get the skill of the version in your go.mod. Other agents read it from any path: mention it in AGENTS.md or in the instructions of the agent.

The skill describes the library, not your project. Keep the rules of your project — where the validators are configured, how the errors are returned to the clients — in your own instructions next to it.

docs.title: Upgrading from v0.0.x
docs.text:
The configuration style is the same, b.String(&u.Name).Required(), but the configurator is typed now. Go 1.27 is required.

v0.0.x Now Configurator[T] is an interface a struct with generic methods, the signature of the Configure function is the same field configurators are interfaces: str.BaseConfigurator, num.BaseConfigurator pointers to concrete types: *str.BaseConfigurator, *num.BaseConfigurator[N], *uuid.BaseConfigurator b.Number(&u.Score) for *int b.NumberPtr(&u.Score) Max(any), Min(any), AnyOf(...any), AnyOfInterval(any, any) the arguments have the type of the field, Max(5) works for int64 Custom(func(ctx, h, value any) ...), When(func(ctx, value any) bool) of fields the value is typed: string, the number type, uuid.UUID Slice(any) with Custom(func(ctx, h, value []*any) ...) Slice[E](*[]E) with Custom(func(ctx, h, value shared.Elems[E]) ...) StringSlice(...).MaxLen(n) the same: the number of elements; rules on elements are set by Each shared.NewSliceFieldConfigurator(params), shared.FieldConfigurator shared.NewSliceFieldConfigurator(field, helper, add), shared.Field[T]

docs.title: Behavior changes
docs.text:
• Validate returns nil for a valid object, it returned an empty slice. Check len(errs) > 0 or errs != nil, both work now.
  • A struct value is validated by a copy, it was silently skipped.
  • Nil pointers and the fields of nil nested structs are skipped by rules, they panicked; Required fails on them.
  • Number(...).Required() fails on zero, it did nothing. NumberPtr(...).Required() fails on nil.
  • AnyOfInterval(begin, end) includes both ends.
  • The errors of slice elements have the index in the location: Tags[1].
  • A field When isn't called for an absent value, it got the zero value.
  • A repeated Configure of the same type replaces its rules, it appended them.

docs.title: Why valigo?
docs.text: valigo is for Go services that validate their input structs and want the rules checked by the compiler, the validation free on valid input, and the messages in the language of the user.

docs.title: Rules are code, checked by the compiler
docs.text:
Rules are configured by pointers to the fields of the model, so the field and its type are known at compile time:

b.String(&u.Name).Required().MaxLen(64)   // String accepts only string and *string fields
b.Number(&u.ID).Min(1)                    // Min takes an int64 for an int64 field
b.Number(&u.ID).Min("1")                  // doesn't compile
b.String(&u.Age)                          // doesn't compile: Age is an int

A renamed field is renamed in the rules by the IDE, a removed field breaks the build instead of a silently skipped rule. Tag based validators keep the rules in strings, validate:"required,max=64", and report a typo or a rule of a wrong type only at runtime.

docs.title: Validation of valid objects doesn't allocate
docs.text: The rules are built once by Configure. Validate reads the fields through precomputed accessors and calls the rules of every field, allocations happen only to build errors. A struct with string, number, uuid and slice rules, conditions and a struct level custom rule is validated with 0 allocations — the tests check it.

docs.title: Absent values are handled, not panicked on
docs.text:
A nil pointer field, a nil pointer to a slice and the fields of a nil nested struct are absent: every rule skips them, only Required fails. Optional fields need no special code:

b.String(&u.Phone).Regexp(phoneRe)  // nil Phone is valid, a set one must match
b.NumberPtr(&u.Discount).Max(50)    // nil Discount is valid
b.String(&u.Address.City).Required() // fails for a nil Address too

docs.title: Conditions and custom rules at every level
docs.text:
When on the struct enables rules by the state of the object, When on a field — by the value of the field. Custom on a field gets its typed value, Custom on the struct gets the whole object and reports errors on any of its fields:

smtp := b.When(func(_ context.Context, s *Sender) bool { return s.Type == "smtp" })
smtp.String(&s.Host).Required()
smtp.Number(&s.Port).AnyOfInterval(1, 65535)

See Conditions and Custom rules.

docs.title: Translated messages
docs.text: Messages of the built-in rules are translated to English and Russian, your own messages are added to the same storage. The language is taken from the context, NewAcceptLanguageMiddleware puts the languages of the Accept-Language header there. See Translations.

docs.title: Errors that point to the field
docs.text: Every error has the message, the location and the value: Tags[1] for an element of a slice, Address.City for a nested field, or the JSON path of the field with a custom location function. See Errors.

docs.title: When valigo is not the right tool
docs.text:
• Rules come from the data, e.g. a form builder or rules stored in a database: valigo rules are Go code compiled into the service.
  • The input is not a struct: valigo validates structs, decode maps and JSON into a struct first.
  • Go older than 1.27: the configurator uses generic methods.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: This page is for the contributors and for those who want to know the cost of a rule.

docs.title: Configure: from pointers to fields
docs.text:
Configure[T] creates the model, a *T with all exported nested structs stored by pointer allocated (pointers to the types being allocated are left nil, so recursive types stop). The model gives every field a unique address, so a pointer &u.Address.City identifies the field: fmap finds the field descriptor by the address relative to the model.

The descriptor knows the offset of the field and the chain of the nested pointer structs, so it reads the field of any object of the type: Address.City of a *User follows the Address pointer and returns a typed nil pointer when it is nil. That's how absent values appear.

docs.title: Typed rules
docs.text:
Configurator methods are generic: String[F ~string | *string](p *F), Number[N num.Number](p *N). The type of the pointer selects the method and the types of the rule arguments, so a wrong field or argument type doesn't compile.

Every field configurator is a thin wrapper over one core type, shared.Field[T]. It has four primitives, all built-in rules are made of them:

Primitive Behavior Check(ok, key, args...) an error with the key when ok(value) is false, absent values are skipped Required(ok, key) an error when the value is absent or ok(value) is false Modify(fn) changes the value in place, e.g. Trim Custom(fn) your function with the typed value and the field helper

When(cond) wraps the next rules of the field with the condition. MaxLen of a string is Check(func(v string) bool { return len(v) <= n }, ...).

shared.Field[T] doesn't know where the value comes from. For a struct field the source reads the field, for Each the source iterates over the elements of the slice and adds the index to the locations of the errors. That's why the same string configurator validates a Name string field and every element of Tags []*string.

docs.title: Validate: the hot path
docs.text:
Configure registers one validation function per field source in the validator, keyed by the type *T. Validate:

  1. finds the functions of the type of the object, a map lookup;
  2. calls every function: it reads the field once through the descriptor, a pointer into the object, and runs the rules of the field;
  3. a rule returns nil for a valid value, and builds a shared.Error with the translated message otherwise.

Nothing in this path allocates for valid objects: the values are read by pointers, the rules are closures created by Configure, the regexps are compiled once, and the helper of struct Custom rules is pooled. A test checks it with testing.AllocsPerRun.

docs.title: Absent values
docs.text:
A value is absent when there is nothing to check:

  • a nil pointer field: *string, *int, *uuid.UUID;
  • a nil pointer to a slice: *[]string;
  • a field of a nested struct stored by a nil pointer: City of a nil *Address;
  • a nil element of a slice of pointers: []*string{nil}.

Every rule skips absent values, only Required fails on them. So an optional field needs no special code: the rules check it only when it is set.

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
)

type Address struct {
    City string
}

type Order struct {
    Comment  *string
    Discount *int
    Coupons  *[]string
    Delivery *Address
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Order](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Order], o *Order) {
        b.String(&o.Comment).MaxLen(200)
        b.NumberPtr(&o.Discount).AnyOfInterval(1, 50)
        b.StringSlice(&o.Coupons).MaxLen(3)
        b.String(&o.Delivery.City).Required()
    })

    // nothing is set: only the Required rule fails
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Order{}))

    discount := 70
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Order{Discount: &discount, Delivery: &Address{City: "Paris"}}))
}

Output:

[Should be fulfilled (Delivery.City: <nil>)]
[Only interval[1 - 50] is allowed (Discount: 70)]

docs.title: Required
docs.text:
What Required checks depends on the type:

Configurator Fails on String absent value, empty string Number zero NumberPtr absent value; zero is a valid value of a pointer UUID absent value, uuid.Nil Slice, StringSlice, UUIDSlice absent slice, empty slice

Nil slices of value fields ([]string(nil)) are present and empty: length rules check them, Each has nothing to check.

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text: A field When doesn't call its condition for an absent value and skips its rules, including Required: the condition is about the value, and there is no value. Put Required before When, or use When of the struct, if the field is required under a condition. See Conditions.

docs.title: When on the struct
docs.text:
When of the configurator returns a configurator whose rules are applied only if the function returns true for the validated object:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
)

type Sender struct {
    Type     string
    SMTPHost string
    SMTPPort int
    HTTPURL  string
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Sender](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Sender], s *Sender) {
        b.String(&s.Type).AnyOf("smtp", "http")

        smtp := b.When(func(_ context.Context, s *Sender) bool { return s.Type == "smtp" })
        smtp.String(&s.SMTPHost).Required()
        smtp.Number(&s.SMTPPort).AnyOfInterval(1, 65535)

        http := b.When(func(_ context.Context, s *Sender) bool { return s.Type == "http" })
        http.String(&s.HTTPURL).Required()
    })

    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Sender{Type: "smtp"}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Sender{Type: "http"}))
}

Output:

[Should be fulfilled (SMTPHost: ) Only interval[1 - 65535] is allowed (SMTPPort: 0)]
[Should be fulfilled (HTTPURL: )]
  • The returned configurator has all methods of the original one, the conditions of chained When calls are combined with AND: b.When(a).When(b).
  • When doesn't change the configurator it is called on: b keeps adding unconditional rules.
  • The context passed to Validate is passed to the condition, e.g. to enable rules by the role of the user.

docs.title: When on a field
docs.text:
When of a field configurator returns a configurator of the same field whose rules are applied only if the function returns true for the value of the field. The rules before When stay unconditional:

b.String(&u.Website).
    Trim().                                                                  // always
    When(func(_ context.Context, v string) bool { return v != "" }).
    Regexp(urlRe)                                                            // only for a non-empty value

The value is typed: string for String, the number type for Number and NumberPtr, uuid.UUID for UUID, and shared.Elems[E] for slices, see Slices.

For an absent value the condition isn't called and the rules after it are skipped, including Required.

docs.title: Conditions and custom rules
docs.text: A condition on several fields can also be written as a struct custom rule, which reports errors itself. Prefer When: the rules after it are the regular ones, with their messages and translations.

docs.title: Validator
docs.text:
valigo.New creates a validator. It holds the rules of all configured types and the translator of the messages, create one per application and share it.

v := valigo.New(
    valigo.WithTranslator(t),                     // translator of the messages, see Translations
    valigo.WithFieldLocationNamingFn(jsonPath),   // location of the field in errors, see Errors
    valigo.WithErrorsTransformer(toProblemFields), // []shared.Error to []error for Validate, see Errors
)

All options are optional, a nil argument keeps the default.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
valigo.Configure[T] configures the rules of the struct type T:

valigo.Configure[User](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[User], u *User) {
    b.String(&u.Name).Required()
})

The function is called once, with:

  • b — the configurator of T, its methods return the configurators of fields: String, Number and NumberPtr, UUID, Slice, StringSlice and UUIDSlice, and When and Custom of the struct;
  • u — the model, a *User created by Configure. Rules are bound to the fields of the model by their pointers.

The rules are applied to objects of type *T: v.Validate(ctx, &user). A struct value is validated too, by a copy, see Errors.

Configure is called on the application start. It isn't safe to call concurrently with Validate, and it panics on invalid configuration: a configuration error is a bug of the code, not a state of the running service. A repeated Configure of the same type replaces its rules.

docs.title: Field pointers
docs.text:
A field pointer must point to a field of the model passed to the function:

valigo.Configure[User](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[User], u *User) {
    b.String(&u.Name)       // a field of the model
    b.String(&u.Address.City) // a field of a nested struct of the model

    var name string
    b.String(&name)         // panic: *string is not a pointer to a field of *main.User: field not found
})

Types of the fields are checked by the compiler: String accepts *string, **string and pointers to named string types, Number accepts pointers to numbers, and so on. Rules can't be configured on a field of a wrong type.

docs.title: Nested structs
docs.text:
Fields of nested structs are configured by the same pointers. The model allocates all nested structs stored by pointer, so &u.Address.City is valid even if Address is *Address:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
)

type Address struct {
    City string
}

type User struct {
    Name    string
    Home    Address
    Work    *Address
    Manager *User // recursive types are supported, the model doesn't allocate Manager
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[User](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[User], u *User) {
        b.String(&u.Home.City).Required()
        b.String(&u.Work.City).Required()
    })

    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &User{Work: &Address{}}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &User{Home: Address{City: "Berlin"}}))
}

Output:

[Should be fulfilled (Home.City: ) Should be fulfilled (Work.City: )]
[Should be fulfilled (Work.City: <nil>)]

When the validated object has a nil Work, the field Work.City is absent: rules skip it and Required fails, see Absent values.

Embedded structs work the same way, &u.ID for a field of an embedded Base. Unexported fields are allowed in the model, and unexported fields of the model itself can be configured too.

docs.title: Reusing rules
docs.text:
Rules of nested types aren't inherited: configuring Address doesn't add its rules to User. Share the rules by a function:

func addressRules[T any](b valigo.Configurator[T], a *Address) {
    b.String(&a.City).Required()
}

valigo.Configure[User](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[User], u *User) {
    addressRules(b, &u.Home)
    addressRules(b, u.Work)
})

docs.title: Field rules
docs.text:
Custom of a field configurator adds a rule with your logic. The function gets the typed value of the field and a helper that builds errors with the location of the field:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "strings"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
)

type Account struct {
    Login string
    Age   int
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Account](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Account], a *Account) {
        b.String(&a.Login).Required().Custom(func(ctx context.Context, h *shared.FieldCustomHelper, login string) []shared.Error {
            if strings.EqualFold(login, "admin") {
                return []shared.Error{h.ErrorT(ctx, login, "Login %q is reserved", login)}
            }
            return nil
        })
        b.Number(&a.Age).Custom(func(ctx context.Context, h *shared.FieldCustomHelper, age int) []shared.Error {
            if age%2 != 0 {
                return []shared.Error{h.ErrorT(ctx, age, "Should be even")}
            }
            return nil
        })
    })

    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Account{Login: "Admin", Age: 3}))
}

Output:

[Login "Admin" is reserved (Login: Admin) Should be even (Age: 3)]

h.ErrorT(ctx, value, localeKey, args...) translates the message: localeKey is looked up in the translations, a key without a translation is used as is, as a format for args.

The function isn't called for an absent value.

docs.title: Rules on slice elements
docs.text:
The Each of Slice gives a *shared.Field[E] of the elements. Besides Custom and When it has Check, the base of all built-in rules: a predicate and a message for the elements that don't match it.

b.Slice(&o.Quantities).Each(func(q *shared.Field[int]) {
    q.Check(func(v int) bool { return v > 0 }, "Should be positive")
})

Required(ok, localeKey) fails for absent elements and the elements that don't match ok, Modify(fn) changes the elements in place. See Slices.

docs.title: Struct rules
docs.text:
Custom of the struct configurator gets the whole object, for the rules on several fields. h.ErrorT takes the pointer to the field of the validated object to build its location:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "time"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
)

type Booking struct {
    From time.Time
    To   time.Time
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Booking](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Booking], _ *Booking) {
        b.Custom(func(ctx context.Context, h shared.StructCustomHelper, obj *Booking) []shared.Error {
            if !obj.To.After(obj.From) {
                return []shared.Error{h.ErrorT(ctx, &obj.To, obj.To.Format(time.DateOnly), "Should be after %s", obj.From.Format(time.DateOnly))}
            }
            return nil
        })
    })

    from := time.Date(2026, 5, 10, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Booking{From: from, To: from.AddDate(0, 0, -1)}))
}

Output:

[Should be after 2026-05-10 (To: 2026-05-09)]
  • Struct Custom can be combined with When: b.When(cond).Custom(fn).
  • The helper is valid only during the call of the function, don't keep it.
  • A pointer that doesn't point to a field of the validated object panics.

docs.title: Validate and ValidateTyped
docs.text:
func (v *Validator) Validate(ctx context.Context, obj any) []error
func (v *Validator) ValidateTyped(ctx context.Context, obj any) []shared.Error
  • ValidateTyped returns the errors as shared.Error values, Validate passes them through the errors transformer, by default every shared.Error becomes an error.
  • Both return nil when the object is valid, when the type of the object has no rules, and for a nil pointer.
  • obj is a pointer to the configured struct. A struct value is validated too, by a shallow copy: Trim of its fields isn't visible to the caller, but the values behind its pointers and the elements of its slices are shared with the caller and can be changed.
  • The errors go in the order of the configuration: the rules of a field in the order of the chain, the fields in the order of their first rule.

docs.title: shared.Error
docs.text:
type Error struct {
    Message  string // translated message
    Location string // location of the field, Address.City or Tags[1] by default
    Value    any    // the checked value, nil for absent values
}

Error() returns Message (Location: Value), or Message alone when both the location and the value are empty. Error has JSON field names of its own: {"Message":"...","Location":"...","Value":...}, convert it to your API format by the transformer.

docs.title: Location of fields
docs.text:
The location is the path of the field in the struct by default: Address.City. WithFieldLocationNamingFn replaces it, e.g. with the path of the JSON tags, so the client sees the names of its request:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/fmap/v3"
    "github.com/insei/valigo"
)

type Address struct {
    City string `json:"city"`
}

type SignUp struct {
    Email   string   `json:"email"`
    Address Address  `json:"address"`
    Tags    []string `json:"tags"`
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New(valigo.WithFieldLocationNamingFn(func(field fmap.Field) string {
        return field.GetTagPath("json", false)
    }))
    valigo.Configure[SignUp](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[SignUp], s *SignUp) {
        b.String(&s.Email).Email()
        b.String(&s.Address.City).Required()
        b.StringSlice(&s.Tags).Email()
    })

    for _, err := range v.ValidateTyped(context.Background(), &SignUp{Email: "a", Tags: []string{"b"}}) {
        fmt.Println(err.Location, err.Message)
    }
}

Output:

email Should be email address
address.city Should be fulfilled
tags[0] Should be email address

The index of a slice element is appended to the location returned by the function.

docs.title: Errors transformer
docs.text:
WithErrorsTransformer sets how Validate converts the errors, e.g. to one error of the API:

type FieldError struct {
    Field   string `json:"field"`
    Message string `json:"message"`
}

type ValidationError struct {
    Fields []FieldError `json:"fields"`
}

func (e *ValidationError) Error() string { return "validation failed" }

v := valigo.New(valigo.WithErrorsTransformer(func(errs []shared.Error) []error {
    fields := make([]FieldError, len(errs))
    for i, err := range errs {
        fields[i] = FieldError{Field: err.Location, Message: err.Message}
    }
    return []error{&ValidationError{Fields: fields}}
}))

The transformer is called only when there are errors.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
Number configures the rules of a numeric field, NumberPtr — of a pointer to a numeric field. Supported types are int, int8, int16, int32, int64, uint, uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64, float32, float64 and named types based on them.

The arguments of the rules have the type of the field. Untyped constants fit any numeric type, a value of another type doesn't compile:

type Price int64

type Product struct {
    Stock    int
    Price    Price
    Rating   float32
    Discount *uint8
}

b.Number(&p.Stock).Min(0)
b.Number(&p.Price).AnyOfInterval(1, 1_000_000) // the arguments are Price
b.Number(&p.Rating).Max(5)
b.NumberPtr(&p.Discount).Max(90)               // a nil Discount is skipped

var limit int32 = 10
b.Number(&p.Stock).Max(limit) // doesn't compile: int32 isn't int

docs.title: Rules
docs.text: Rule Fails when Message Required() Number: the value is zero; NumberPtr: the value is absent Should be fulfilled Min(n) the value is less than n Cannot be less than %v Max(n) the value is greater than n Cannot be greater than %v AnyOf(values...) the value isn't one of values Only %v values is allowed AnyOfInterval(begin, end) the value is outside [begin, end], both ends are included Only interval[%v - %v] is allowed Custom(fn) fn returns errors your messages, see Custom rules When(fn) — the next rules are applied only if fn returns true, see Conditions

docs.title: Zero and absent
docs.text:
Zero is a valid value of a pointer: NumberPtr(&p.Discount).Required() passes for a pointer to 0 and fails for nil. Use a pointer field when zero must be distinguished from "not set", e.g. in PATCH requests:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
)

type UpdateProduct struct {
    Stock *int
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[UpdateProduct](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[UpdateProduct], p *UpdateProduct) {
        b.NumberPtr(&p.Stock).Min(0)
    })

    zero, negative := 0, -1
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &UpdateProduct{}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &UpdateProduct{Stock: &zero}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &UpdateProduct{Stock: &negative}))
}

Output:

[]
[]
[Cannot be less than 0 (Stock: -1)]

docs.title: Slices
docs.text: Configurator Fields Rules on elements Slice []E of any E Each with *shared.Field[E]: Check, Required, Modify, Custom, When StringSlice []string, *[]string, []*string, *[]*string Each with the string configurator, Trim, Regexp, Email UUIDSlice []uuid.UUID, *[]uuid.UUID, []*uuid.UUID, *[]*uuid.UUID Each with the uuid configurator, AnyOf

docs.title: The slice and its elements
docs.text:
The rules of the configurator check the slice itself, the rules inside Each check every element:

Rule Fails when Message Required() the slice is absent or empty Should be fulfilled MinLen(n) the slice has less than n elements Cannot contain less than %d elements MaxLen(n) the slice has more than n elements Cannot contain more than %d elements Each(fn) — fn configures the rules of the elements

Trim, Regexp and Email of StringSlice and AnyOf of UUIDSlice are shortcuts for the same rules in Each.

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/google/uuid"
    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
    vuuid "github.com/insei/valigo/uuid"
)

type Post struct {
    Tags       []string
    Editors    []*uuid.UUID
    Quantities []int
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Post](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Post], p *Post) {
        b.StringSlice(&p.Tags).Required().MaxLen(3).Each(func(tag *str.BaseConfigurator) {
            tag.Trim().Required().MaxLen(10)
        })
        b.UUIDSlice(&p.Editors).Each(func(id *vuuid.BaseConfigurator) {
            id.Required()
        })
        b.Slice(&p.Quantities).Each(func(q *shared.Field[int]) {
            q.Check(func(v int) bool { return v > 0 }, "Should be positive")
        })
    })

    editor := uuid.MustParse("6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8")
    post := &Post{
        Tags:       []string{"go", "  ", "validation-library"},
        Editors:    []*uuid.UUID{&editor, nil},
        Quantities: []int{1, 0},
    }
    for _, err := range v.Validate(context.Background(), post) {
        fmt.Println(err)
    }
}

Output:

Should be fulfilled (Tags[1]: )
Cannot be longer than 10 characters (Tags[2]: validation-library)
Should be fulfilled (Editors[1]: <nil>)
Should be positive (Quantities[1]: 0)

The location of an element error has the index of the element, the errors of the slice itself have the location of the field. Nil elements of slices of pointers are absent: only Required fails on them.

docs.title: Custom and When
docs.text:
Custom and When of the slice configurators get the elements as shared.Elems[E], a view over []E and []*E without copying:

b.StringSlice(&p.Tags).Custom(func(ctx context.Context, h *shared.FieldCustomHelper, tags shared.Elems[string]) []shared.Error {
    seen := make(map[string]bool, tags.Len())
    for _, tag := range tags.All() { // tag is *string, nil for nil elements of []*string
        if tag != nil && seen[*tag] {
            return []shared.Error{h.ErrorT(ctx, *tag, "Tags should be unique")}
        }
        if tag != nil {
            seen[*tag] = true
        }
    }
    return nil
})

Len() returns the number of elements, At(i) the pointer to the element i, All() iterates over the indexes and the pointers.

docs.title: Slices of pointers in Slice
docs.text:
Slice works with the declared element type: for []*int the element is *int, and nil elements are regular values for its rules:

b.Slice(&p.Limits).Each(func(limit *shared.Field[*int]) {
    limit.Check(func(v *int) bool { return v != nil }, "Should be set")
})

docs.title: Strings
docs.text:
String configures the rules of a string field, a *string field or a field of a named string type:

type Status string

type User struct {
    Name     string
    Nickname *string
    Status   Status
}

b.String(&u.Name).Trim().Required().MaxLen(64)
b.String(&u.Nickname).MinLen(3) // a nil Nickname is skipped
b.String(&u.Status).AnyOf("active", "blocked")

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Rule Fails when Message Required() the value is absent or empty Should be fulfilled MinLen(n) the length is less than n Cannot be shorter than %d characters MaxLen(n) the length is greater than n Cannot be longer than %d characters AnyOf(values...) the value isn't one of values Only %s values is allowed Regexp(re, opts...) the value doesn't match re Doesn't match required regexp pattern Email() the value isn't an email address Should be email address Custom(fn) fn returns errors your messages, see Custom rules When(fn) — the next rules are applied only if fn returns true, see Conditions

The lengths are in bytes, like len: "яя" has the length 4.

docs.title: Trim
docs.text:
Trim() removes the leading and trailing whitespace of the value in the validated object. Rules run in the order of the chain, so the rules after Trim check the trimmed value:

b.String(&u.Name).Trim().Required() // "   " fails, "  Ann " becomes "Ann"

The struct is validated in place, Validate(ctx, &user) trims user.Name. See the copy semantics of the values passed by value in Errors.

docs.title: Regexp message
docs.text:
str.WithRegexpLocaleKey replaces the message of a Regexp rule, the key can have its own translations:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "regexp"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
)

type Product struct {
    SKU string
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Product](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Product], p *Product) {
        b.String(&p.SKU).Regexp(regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}$`), str.WithRegexpLocaleKey("Should look like ABC-1234"))
    })
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Product{SKU: "abc-1"}))
}

Output:

[Should look like ABC-1234 (SKU: abc-1)]

docs.title: Translations
docs.text: Messages are translated by a translator.Translator. The default one of valigo.New has the English and Russian messages of the built-in rules, English is the default language.

docs.title: Locale keys
docs.text:
The rules build messages by locale keys: validation:string:Cannot be longer than %d characters. The translator looks the key up in the languages of the context, then in the default language, and formats the found message with the arguments of the rule. A key without a translation is used as is: so the messages of custom rules work without translations.

The keys of the built-in rules are in translator/locales:

validation:
  string:
    "Cannot be longer than %d characters": Не может быть длиннее %d символов

docs.title: Languages from the context
docs.text:
The languages of the request are taken from the context, translator.NewAcceptLanguageMiddleware puts the languages of the Accept-Language header there, ordered by their q:

handler := translator.NewAcceptLanguageMiddleware()(mux)

Another source of the languages is set by translator.WithPreferredLanguagesFn, e.g. the language of the user profile.

docs.title: Own messages
docs.text:
Add the translations of your messages to a storage and pass the translator to the validator:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/translator"
)

type language struct{}

type Account struct {
    Login string
}

const reservedKey = "validation:login:Login %q is reserved"

func main() {
    storage := translator.NewInMemStorage() // the built-in locales are loaded
    storage.Add("en", map[string]string{reservedKey: "Login %q is reserved"})
    storage.Add("ru", map[string]string{reservedKey: "Логин %q зарезервирован"})

    t := translator.New(
        translator.WithStorage(storage),
        translator.WithDefaultLang("en"),
        translator.WithPreferredLanguagesFn(func(ctx context.Context) []string {
            lang, _ := ctx.Value(language{}).(string)
            return []string{lang}
        }),
    )

    v := valigo.New(valigo.WithTranslator(t))
    valigo.Configure[Account](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Account], a *Account) {
        b.String(&a.Login).MinLen(3).Custom(func(ctx context.Context, h *shared.FieldCustomHelper, login string) []shared.Error {
            if login == "root" {
                return []shared.Error{h.ErrorT(ctx, login, reservedKey, login)}
            }
            return nil
        })
    })

    ctx := context.WithValue(context.Background(), language{}, "ru")
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(ctx, &Account{Login: "ro"}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(ctx, &Account{Login: "root"}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Account{Login: "root"}))
}

Output:

[Не может быть короче 3 символов (Login: ro)]
[Логин "root" зарезервирован (Login: root)]
[Login "root" is reserved (Login: root)]
  • storage.Merge(locales) adds the translations of several languages at once, e.g. from your own YAML files read by translator.LocalesFromFS(fsys): locales/<lang>/data.yaml with the same nested format as the built-in locales.
  • translator.NewInMemStorage(translator.WithInMemData(data)) replaces the built-in locales with yours.
  • str.WithRegexpLocaleKey sets the key of a Regexp rule.

docs.title: UUID
docs.text:
UUID configures the rules of a uuid.UUID field or a *uuid.UUID field:

type Comment struct {
    ID       uuid.UUID
    ParentID *uuid.UUID
}

b.UUID(&c.ID).Required()
b.UUID(&c.ParentID).Custom(notDeleted) // a nil ParentID is skipped

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Rule Fails when Message Required() the value is absent or uuid.Nil Should be fulfilled AnyOf(values...) the value isn't one of values Only %s values is allowed Custom(fn) fn returns errors your messages, see Custom rules When(fn) — the next rules are applied only if fn returns true, see Conditions

Slices of uuids are configured by UUIDSlice, see Slices.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/google/uuid"
    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
)

type Comment struct {
    ID       uuid.UUID
    ParentID *uuid.UUID
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Comment](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Comment], c *Comment) {
        b.UUID(&c.ID).Required().Custom(func(ctx context.Context, h *shared.FieldCustomHelper, id uuid.UUID) []shared.Error {
            if id.Version() != 7 {
                return []shared.Error{h.ErrorT(ctx, id, "Should be UUID v7")}
            }
            return nil
        })
    })

    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Comment{}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Comment{ID: uuid.MustParse("6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8")}))
}

Output:

[Should be fulfilled (ID: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000) Should be UUID v7 (ID: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000)]
[Should be UUID v7 (ID: 6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8)]
